title: Relationship quiz: how healthy is your relationship? Free test — cv.cm
description: Free relationship quiz: rate 14 statements about trust, respect, communication, support and conflict to see how healthy your relationship is, with a score from 0 to 56 and tips. Private, no sign-up.
lede: Do you feel safe, heard and supported, or are you walking on eggshells? Rate 14 statements about trust, respect, communication and conflict to see how healthy your relationship looks right now.
about: Healthy relationships come in many shapes, but they share a few things: trust, respect, honest communication, support for each other's goals, fairness, and disagreements that get worked out rather than turned into attacks. Every couple has hard patches. What matters more is whether you can be yourself, raise problems safely and repair things after a fight. Warning signs include feeling you must watch what you say, constant checking of your phone or whereabouts, insults, being cut off from friends, and feeling afraid of how your partner will react.

The statements here were written for cv.cm around those signs and work for any couple, whether dating, living together or married. They are not a published scale, half of them describe warning signs, and the score is a rough picture, not a verdict on your relationship. Whatever your score, if you feel afraid of your partner, or they hurt, threaten or control you, that is abuse, not a rough patch: please reach out to a domestic violence helpline, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

faq.q: How is the score worked out?
faq.a: Each statement scores 0 to 4, and the warning-sign statements are reversed, so the total runs from 0 to 56. 18 or less looks strained, 19 to 37 is a mix and 38 or more looks healthy.

faq.q: What are the signs of a healthy relationship?
faq.a: You trust each other, feel free to be yourselves, talk openly about problems, support each other's goals, share the load fairly and still enjoy time together.

faq.q: What if I feel afraid of my partner?
faq.a: Take that seriously, whatever your score. Fear, threats, control over your phone, money or friends, and any violence are signs of abuse. A domestic violence helpline can talk it through in confidence, and in an emergency call your local emergency number.

faq.q: Can my partner and I take it together?
faq.a: Yes. Take it separately, then compare where you agreed and where you didn't. The differences are often the best place to start a conversation, or to bring to a couples counselor.

items: I trust my partner, and I feel they trust me.
I often feel I have to watch what I say around my partner.
We can disagree without it turning into a fight.
Our arguments often end in insults, yelling or the silent treatment.
My partner supports my goals, even when they're different from theirs.
My partner checks my phone, messages or whereabouts more than I'm comfortable with.
I feel I can be completely myself with my partner.
I often feel lonely in this relationship.
We share the work of our home and our life fairly.
One of us almost always gets the final say.
We still make time for each other and have fun together.
I've given up friends or activities I enjoyed because of my partner.
When something bothers me, I can bring it up and we talk it through.
I sometimes feel afraid of how my partner will react.

strained.name: Your relationship looks strained (0–18)
strained.body: Your answers show many warning signs: trust, respect or safe communication seem to be missing much of the time. That's painful, and you deserve better. If you feel afraid of your partner, or they hurt, threaten or control you, please contact a domestic violence helpline, and in an emergency call your local emergency number. If it's more about distance and conflict, a couples counselor can help you both decide what comes next.

mixed.name: Some strengths, some strain (19–37)
mixed.body: Your relationship has real strengths alongside some patterns that wear it down. Look at the statements you disagreed with: they show where to focus, whether that's how you argue, how decisions get made or how much time you spend together. Talk about one of them when things are calm. If any answer was about fear or control, take it seriously whatever your score.

healthy.name: Your relationship looks healthy (38–56)
healthy.body: Your answers show a lot of trust, respect and good communication: you can be yourself, raise problems and get through disagreements. Keep investing in it, with time together, curiosity about each other and repair after small fights. Every relationship goes through hard seasons; the habits you have now will help you through them.
